marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q001.takeaway: Pharynx extends from cranial base to lower cricoid border around C6.
marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q001.displayText: The lower border of the pharynx is at the level of C6 (the source explanation also notes C6/C7). The pharynx extends from the cranial base to the lower border of the cricoid cartilage and is divided into the nasopharynx, oropharynx, and laryngopharynx.
emphasis: lower border of the cricoid cartilage

rationales.a: C1 is at upper cervical level, far above the inferior end of pharynx.
rationales.b: C2 remains within upper pharynx, not lower cricoid level.
rationales.c: C4 is above lower border; the source gives C6/C7 near cricoid.

marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q002.takeaway: Piriform fossa belongs to laryngopharynx, not nasopharynx.
marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q002.displayText: The piriform fossa is a feature of the laryngopharynx, not the nasopharynx. Structures seen in the nasopharynx include the opening of the eustachian tube, torus tubarius, the fossa of Rosenmuller behind the torus, the pharyngeal tonsil, and Passavant’s ridge. The fossa of Rosenmuller is an important site for nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

rationales.b: Passavant ridge is posterior nasopharynx, not a piriform recess.
rationales.c: Auditory tube opening is a nasopharyngeal structure.
rationales.d: Torus tubarius surrounds the auditory tube opening in nasopharynx.

marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q003.takeaway: Palatopharyngeus with superior constrictor forms Passavant ridge.
marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q003.displayText: Passavant’s ridge is formed by the palatopharyngeus and superior constrictor. Some fibers of palatopharyngeus form an internal sphincter superior to the superior constrictor; contraction produces a ridge on the posterior wall of the nasopharynx.

rationales.a: Levator veli palatini elevates soft palate but is not the source-named pair forming Passavant ridge.
rationales.c: Palatoglossus and middle constrictor are not the posterior wall ridge-forming pair.
rationales.d: Palatoglossus forms anterior faucial arch; superior constrictor and palatopharyngeus create Passavant ridge.

marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q004.takeaway: Pharyngeal opening of auditory tube lies behind posterior end of inferior turbinate.
marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q004.displayText: The symptoms suggest spread to the middle ear through the eustachian tube. Its nasopharyngeal opening lies approximately behind the posterior end of the inferior turbinate on the lateral wall of the nasopharynx. The tube connects the nasopharynx to the middle ear, is normally collapsed, and opens during yawning and swallowing.
emphasis: behind the posterior end of the inferior turbinate

rationales.a: The opening is behind posterior end of inferior turbinate, not middle turbinate.
rationales.c: The tube opens posteriorly on lateral nasopharynx, not anterior to inferior turbinate.
rationales.d: The source landmark is posterior to inferior turbinate, not between the turbinates.

marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q005.takeaway: Passavant ridge is on posterior nasopharynx, outside oropharynx.
marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q005.displayText: The image is consistent with acute tonsillitis. Passavant’s ridge lies on the posterior wall of the nasopharynx and is not an oropharyngeal structure. The oropharynx extends from below the soft palate to the upper border of the epiglottis and includes the palatoglossal folds, palatopharyngeal folds, palatine tonsils between them, lingual tonsils, and valleculae.

rationales.a: Palatopharyngeal folds are visible in oropharynx.
rationales.b: Palatine tonsils lie between palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal folds in oropharynx.
rationales.d: Palatoglossal folds mark the anterior oropharynx; Passavant ridge lies higher on posterior nasopharynx.

marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q006.takeaway: Valleculae are oropharyngeal, not hypopharyngeal landmarks.
marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q006.displayText: Valleculae belong to the oropharynx and are not part of the hypopharynx. The hypopharynx or laryngopharynx extends from the superior border of the epiglottis to the lower border of the cricoid cartilage. Its landmarks include the laryngeal inlet, posterior pharyngeal wall, postcricoid region, and piriform fossae. The piriform fossa lies between the aryepiglottic fold medially and the thyroid cartilage/thyrohyoid membrane laterally; internal laryngeal branches run beneath its mucosa.

rationales.a: Piriform fossa is a laryngopharyngeal recess and is visible in hypopharynx.
rationales.b: Postcricoid region is part of laryngopharynx.
rationales.d: Posterior pharyngeal wall extends through hypopharynx; valleculae lie between tongue base and epiglottis in oropharynx.

marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q007.takeaway: Sinus of Morgagni lies between skull base and upper edge of superior constrictor.
marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q007.displayText: The sinus of Morgagni is the gap between the skull base and the upper border of the superior constrictor. It transmits the palatine branch of the ascending pharyngeal artery, ascending palatine artery, levator veli palatini, and the eustachian tube. The source also notes Trotter’s triad in nasopharyngeal carcinoma: conductive hearing loss, ipsilateral palatal immobility, and neuralgic pain.
emphasis: upper border of the superior constrictor

rationales.a: This describes Laimer/Killian region lower in pharynx, not the skull-base gap for sinus of Morgagni.
rationales.b: Superior and middle constrictors are lower than the gap beneath skull base.
rationales.d: Below inferior constrictor is esophageal region; sinus of Morgagni is superior.

marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q008.takeaway: Killian dehiscence in inferior constrictor predisposes to Zenker diverticulum.
marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q008.displayText: The finding is a Zenker diverticulum, which protrudes through Killian’s dehiscence in the inferior constrictor. The upper thyropharyngeus has oblique fibers and the lower cricopharyngeus has transverse fibers; the weak area between them is Killian’s dehiscence. The source also describes Laimer’s triangle between the cricopharyngeus and longitudinal muscle of the esophagus.

rationales.a: Zenker diverticulum protrudes through Killian dehiscence between thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus portions of inferior constrictor, not superior constrictor.
rationales.c: Middle constrictor is higher and does not contain Killian dehiscence.
rationales.d: Palatopharyngeus contributes to pharyngeal wall but is not the weak inferior-constrictor area.

marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q009.takeaway: Stylopharyngeus is supplied by CN IX, not pharyngeal plexus.
marrow__ANAT_CH33_Q009.displayText: Stylopharyngeus is supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve and is the exception. The pharyngeal plexus is formed by pharyngeal branches of the glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves with sympathetic fibers from the superior cervical ganglion. It supplies the soft-palate muscles except tensor veli palatini, and the pharyngeal muscles except stylopharyngeus.

rationales.a: Palatoglossus is supplied through pharyngeal plexus (vagus), unlike stylopharyngeus.
rationales.c: Middle constrictor is supplied via pharyngeal plexus.
rationales.d: Levator veli palatini is supplied by pharyngeal plexus; stylopharyngeus is CN IX exception.
